business_rules: Movie title is the unique identifier for catalog registration; duplicate titles are prevented (RF-28, RF-35).
Usernames must be unique; duplicate user registration is prevented (RF-34, RNF-43).
A movie can belong to multiple categories (RF-20, RNF-56).
Catalog-management functions are restricted to the administrator role (RF-06, RNF-46).
Access is denied when the user does not exist, the password is incorrect, or the role does not match registration (RF-04).
Uploading the video file and registering the movie are related but independent steps (RNF-57).
Automatic playback depends on an MP4 file corresponding to the registered title (RF-36, RNF-58, RNF-62).
The source movie filename must follow the environment-configured pattern for automatic loading (RNF-59).
If a video file is not in the delivery area, the system attempts to obtain it from the configured local repository (RF-25).
Deletion of nonexistent movies is prevented; batch deletion informs the admin of selected movies first (RF-32, RF-33).
The catalog is displayed in pages of up to 12 movies (RNF-40).
Standard video format is MP4; uploads supported up to 2 GB per file (RNF-48, RNF-49).

microservices.responsibility: Manages user registration, login/logout, session identity, role distinction (regular user vs administrator), and enforces role-based access control for restricted areas. Backed by UserController and user persistence.

Handles movie catalog browsing (paginated listing with title, poster, rating), per-movie details with full metadata and cast, category-based discovery (browse/filter by category, multi-category movies), and administrative catalog management (register, delete single/batch, duplicate-title prevention, confirmation). Backed by MovieController and TypeController over movie and category persistence.

Manages movie video uploads (up to 2 GB MP4), ensures video availability in the delivery area with fallback to the configured local repository, provides playback start and download links based on filename-pattern conventions. Backed by MovieUploadController and file utilities/properties.

issues.description: Catalog administration and video upload are restricted to administrators (RF-06, RF-26, RF-29, RNF-46), and role/access identity is owned by the User and Access Service. Yet the declared interactions have Catalog Service communicating with User and Access Service (good), but Media Delivery Service also lists User and Access Service. The directionality/purpose of authorization is inconsistent: administrative catalog operations in Catalog Service require role validation from the User and Access Service, but this dependency is present, while the enforcement flow is underspecified. More critically, RNF-60 flags that backend authorization is not fully validated, so the design should explicitly route admin-gated operations through the access service rather than leave enforcement implicit.
evidence: aspect package (1 class) as sole server-side gate
issues.recommendation: Make the authorization interaction explicit and correctly directed: Catalog Service and Media Delivery Service must consult the User and Access Service to validate administrator role before executing register/delete/upload operations. Document this as the mechanism satisfying RNF-46 and closing the RNF-60 gap.

issues.description: The Catalog Service bundles browsing (MovieController), category discovery (TypeController), and administration into one service. Category-based discovery is a distinct capability backed by a separate controller (TypeController) and could arguably be its own boundary. This is borderline and defensible given the small codebase and tight domain coupling between movies and categories, but reviewers should note the aggregation.
issues.recommendation: Acceptable to keep merged given the strong movie-category relational coupling and shared persistence, but confirm cohesion is intentional; no split required unless category management grows independently.

preserved_decisions: Separation of Media Delivery Service from Catalog Service is well-supported by MovieUploadController, utils (java.io/java.nio), and properties for file/repository handling (RF-24/25, RNF-48/49/50/51).
User and Access Service backed by UserController and role distinction (RF-01..RF-07, RF-03) is a coherent boundary.
Catalog Service backed by MovieController/TypeController over movie and category persistence is a reasonable domain boundary.
The three-service granularity avoids nanoservices and matches the modest codebase scale (28 classes, single jar).

The missing authorization interaction is the material issue requiring revision.
